reasoning: Justin circulated the Velvet Widow clipping, knew the bottle history and had an admitted solitary visit beside Grant's waiting glass. The real bottle stood uncovered, its closure was split behind the stopper, cyanide remained active, and a similar closure scrap reached the poisoned glass. His final assertion that a later newspaper correction documented neutralization is directly contradicted by the retained correction, which concerns only the former owner's name. This is a false explanation of the murder means rather than merely a defensive account of some unrelated scandal. Grant could discredit Justin's property story using the omitted settlement, providing personal motive. Chip is the strongest competitor: he fitted the matching band, had access and disputes a date which places his work after the contents warning. I cannot exclude him physically. Justin's affirmative attempt to make the source harmless is more specifically useful to a poisoner than Chip's unsupported copying-error defense, so it decides my vote without making the solution conclusive.
feedback: The voices have useful individual habits: Monet's wage urgency, Chip's practical commands and Dada's unexpectedly candid spite work well. Cross-addresses make this feel more social than a lineup of biographies. However, nearly every person follows the same progression from grievance to admitted access to a final qualified denial. That symmetry makes the construction visible and creates a lot of reading for relatively little change in the core poisoning timeline. The six evidence sheets are clean, legible and generously spaced; the seal and wooden-model photographs reward looking. Several sheets are plainly curator summaries rather than convincing recovered documents, especially the consolidated payment and installation checklists. The mystery supports an informed accusation, but I do not see exclusive physical proof against my choice. Distinguishing a murder-serving lie from unrelated wrongdoing does much of the work. Offstage coordinators and service staff are clearly functional witnesses, not confusing extra suspects. No deduction appears to require an absent selectable speaker. Speeches mostly leave interpretation open, though repeating the same bottle and camera conclusions reduces discovery.

issues.detail: Justin's false neutralization claim and Chip's disputed closure date both undermine knowledge defenses, while both retain possible access. Neither supplies exclusive physical linkage to the poisoned glass.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one independently verifiable timing or handling fact that helps separate these competing explanations without naming a culprit.

issues.detail: The opportunity and final rounds repeatedly restate access, documentary contradictions and closed installations across all 22 people.
issues.suggested_fix: Shorten final statements that add no changed admission, relationship or inference.

issues.detail: Method sheets 3 through 5 consolidate unrelated accounts into tidy issue-resolution tables, weakening the feel of recovered museum paperwork.
issues.suggested_fix: Give the most consequential entries their own short source excerpts and retain summaries only as navigation.
